status.en: 111 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 18% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 111 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 18 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits abducted an 11-month-old baby, killed two clerics and attacked a community in Zamfara, while militia groups targeted Irigwe villages in southern Kaduna and gathered around Kainji Lake. The Nigerian army ambushed bandits, killing two and recovering weapons, and troops killed two terrorists and arrested informants linked to a bandit kingpin in Zamfara. A 19-year-old Christian farmer in Nigeria lost a hand in an attack, and a land dispute in Niger state resulted in dozens of deaths. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter bortførte en 11‑måneder gammel baby, drepte to geistlige og angrep et samfunn i Zamfara, mens militsgrupper målrettet Irigwe-landsbyer i sørlige Kaduna og samlet seg rundt Kainji-sjøen. Den nigerianske hæren la en bakholdsangrep på banditter, drepte to og gjenvant våpen, og tropper drepte to terrorister og arresterte informanter knyttet til en banditt-hovedperson i Zamfara. En 19‑år gammel kristen bonde i Nigeria mistet en hånd i et angrep, og en jordkonflikt i Niger-delstaten førte til dusinvis av dødsfall. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
